sentences.text:
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Shri Vijay Vikram Singh, learned counsel for the opposite
party no. 2 and learned A.G.A. for the State.

2. This application u/s 528 Bnss has been filed for quashing of the entire proceedings, including
charge-sheet dated 16.04.2023 as well as cognizance/ summoning order dated 19.04.2023, of
Criminal Case No. 3336 of 2023 (State v. Nanhey Babu and others), arising out of Case Crime No.
389 of 2020, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 474, 504, 506 of Ipc, P.S.- Quila, District- Bareilly,
pending in the court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bareilly.
3.  It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is not named in the First Information Report and he has been falsely implicated during investigation.

Applicant was working Nanhey Babu vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66117135/
1 as 'Lekhpal' and he has merely forwarded the 'Amaldaramad Parwaana' to the computer section for entry in Khatauni.

sentences.text: There is no evidence that applicant has committed any forgery.
As soon as he came to know about the real facts, he has immediately send his report to the higher officers and the alleged order was cancelled.
It was further submitted that co-accused Mohd. Tahir has already filed a writ petition before this Court challenging the order of Nayab Tehsildar, wherein interim order has already been passed.
It is next submitted that applicant has performed his duty in good faith.
Applicant has since retired and no departmental proceedings were initiated against him.
Referring to these facts, it was submitted that no prima facie case is made out against the applicant and the impugned proceedings are malicious and thus, liable to be quashed.
4. Learned AGA and learned counsel for the informant have opposed the application and submitted that during investigation, it was revealed that applicant was involved in the incident.

It was pointed out that during investigation, Sher Bahadur Singh, the then Tehsildar, has made an statement that regarding entry of Parvaana in Khatauni, no application was filed in the Tehsil and that the R-6 Form was prepared by applicant, who was working as 'Lekhpal/ Incharge Revenue Inspector'.
It was also submitted that in inquiry the order dated 13.06.2016 of Consolidation Officer was found forged and thereafter an order was passed for cancellation of entry in Khatauni.
It was stated that applicant was instrumental in making entry on the basis of forged order.
Referring to facts of the matter, it was submitted that applicant was actively involved in entire scenario of incident and a prima facie case is made out against him.
5. I have considered the rival submissions and perused the record.

6. The legal position on the issue of quashing of criminal proceedings is well-settled that the jurisdiction to quash a complaint, FIR or a charge-sheet should be exercised sparingly and only in exceptional cases.

However, where the allegations made in the FIR or the complaint and material on record even if taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused, the charge-sheet may be quashed in exercise of inherent powers under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.

In well celebrated judgement reported in AIR 1992 SC 605 State of Haryana and others Vs. Ch. Bhajan Lal, Supreme Court has carved out certain guidelines, wherein FIR or proceedings may be quashed but cautioned that the power to quash FIR or proceedings should be exercised sparingly and that too in the rarest of rare cases.

entities.text: AIR 1992 SC 605 State of Haryana and others Vs. Ch. Bhajan Lal
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. In the instant matter though the applicant is not named in the First Information Report but during investigation his complicity was revealed.

It was shown that applicant, who was working as 'Lekhpal/ Incharge Revenue Inspector', has made entry in revenue record on the basis of forged order and that no application for such entry was filed in the Tehsil.
There are allegations of forgery and making of entry in revenue record on the basis of forged order.
In view of material on record, it can not be said that no prima-facie case is made out against applicant.
The submissions raised by learned counsel for the applicant call for determination on questions of fact, which may adequately be discerned/adjudicated only by the trial court.
Even the submissions made on point of law can also be more appropriately gone into by the trial court.
Adjudication of questions of facts and appreciation of evidence or examining the reliability and credibility of the version, does not fall within the arena of jurisdiction under Section 528 BNSS.

sentences.text: After considering arguments raised by learned counsel for the parties and perusing the impugned proceedings and the materials in support of the same, this Court does not find it to be a case which can be determined or gone into in an application under Section 528 BNSS.
In view of material on record, no case for quashing of impugned proceedings or any other interference is made out.

Hence,
the present application under Section 528 BNSS is liable to be dismissed.
10. Accordingly, the application u/s 528 BNSS is hereby dismissed.
